title: Analyzing self-assembled spindle dynamics in fission yeast meiosis using in vivo fluorescence imaging
protocol: Take a small amount of frozen biomass from the glycerol stock of cells and place it onto a plate of solid rich medium, such as supplemented yeast extract (YES) medium.
Incubate the plate at a temperature of 25°C to 32°C for 1–2 days until a patch of biomass grows.
Take a small amount of the grown biomass and inoculate it into 5–10 mL of liquid YES medium in a 25–50 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Incubate the culture at a temperature of 25°C to 30°C at 200 rpm until it reaches saturation, typically indicated by an optical density of 1.
Reduce the concentration of glucose from 3% to 1% for partial nutrient starvation.
Dilute the pre-culture in a new flask with a total volume of 10 mL of fresh MM containing 1% glucose.
Grow the culture for approximately 16–20 hours until it reaches an optical density of 0.6–0.8.
Do not dilute this pre-culture to an initial O.D lower than 0.01 to avoid poor fission yeast inoculum issues.
Plate out cells onto solid MEA medium after growing them in liquid culture under partial glucose deprivation for a more synchronous induction of cell conjugation.
Incubate the cells on solid MEA medium for 4–6 hours to initiate meiosis.
Transfer the culture from its current vessel to a 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge the culture at 1000 × g for 3 min.
Discard the supernatant from the centrifuged culture.
Wash the pellet by pipetting an equal volume of minimal medium without nitrogen (2% glucose) onto the pellet.
Centrifuge the culture once again at 1000 × g for 3 min.
Discard the supernatant from the centrifuged culture.
Use a pipette to remove any remaining liquid.
Resuspend the pellet in 100–150 μL of liquid minimal medium without nitrogen, adjusting the volume according to the size of the pellet.
Place a 10 μL drop of the resuspended pellet onto a plate of MEA medium.
Allow the drop to dry.
Incubate the plate at a temperature of 28°C for 4–6 h.
Add 10 μL of soy lectin (1 mg/mL) to the center of an iBidi 8-well μ-slide or 50 μL for an iBidi 35 mm high μ-Dish and allow it to settle for 2 min.
Use a pipette to extract as much of the lectin as possible from the chamber, then allow the remaining residue to air dry.
Gently resuspend a small amount of biomass from the MEA plate in 300 μL of MM-N using a 1 mL pipette tip.
Immobolize the cells by placing 100 μL of the prepared suspension onto the lectin-coated microscopy chamber.
Allow the cells to settle for 4 minutes.
Wash away non-immobilized cells by adding 300 μL of fresh MM-N from one side towards the cell spot in an iBidi 8-well μ-slide.
Discard the washing medium after adding 300 μL of fresh MM-N.
Repeat the washing step three times, discarding the washing medium each time.
Add either 300 μL of MM-N for the iBidi 8-well μ-slide after completing the washes.
For the iBidi 35 mm high μ-Dish, add 1 mL of fresh MM-N from one side towards the cell spot at the bottom of the dish to wash away non-immobilized cells.
Repeat the washing step three times for the iBidi 35 mm high μ-Dish, discarding the washing medium each time.
Add either 1 mL of MM-N for the iBidi 35 mm high μ-Dish after completing the washes.
Set the required temperature in the microscope to 28°C at least 3 hours before starting the timelapse.
Prepare the necessary hardware for the microscopy system.
Initiate the microscopy software program.
Select the 100× objective with immersion oil capability on the microscope.
Apply a drop of immersion oil onto the selected objective.
Insert the microscopy chamber into the microscope stage using the appropriate adapter.
Ensure that the medium is accessible for adding drugs if necessary.
Move the objective towards the bottom of the chamber until you reach the focal plane where the cells are immobilized.
Choose multiple non-overlapping positions throughout the spot of previously immobilized cells to obtain the maximum number of meiocytes per field.
Familiarize yourself with the setup of your microscopy system and understand the risks of photobleaching or phototoxicity due to fluorescence cross-incidence radiation between close positions.
Confirm that all positions remain in focus using a brightfield view before initiating the timelapse.
Re-focus any defocused positions.
Activate the required laser lines and ensure they pass through the sample.
Add the necessary volume of drug to the medium before starting the timelapse.
Ensure the drug is added on top of the medium surface.
Monitor a live brightfield view of a selected position during drug addition to check for drifting.
Initiate the timelapse acquisition.
Examine the acquired microscopy images to ensure they meet quality criteria for subsequent analysis.
Create a maximum projection of all Z planes for each position across all time points to obtain an initial overview of the timelapse.
Carefully review the entire timelapse for any events that could affect microscopy analysis.
Verify that the range of acquired Z planes covers the entire vertical range of fluorescently labeled structures for each channel.
Identify appropriate meiocytes and conduct an analysis of the structures of interest, primarily focusing on chromosomes and microtubules (the spindle).
Examine each individual plane in the Z stack to ensure that there is minimal overlap of the signal captured by that plane and its adjacent planes in the maximum projection.
Measure the length of the spindle body.
